- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 7–14 days.  
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion after 10+ consecutive days of high prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day if price >90% of 30d moving avg.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights early sentiment; adjust by reducing first 5–7 days’ forecast if sentiment is high or volatile.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.5, 0.0, 0.5), model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for smoothing.
